Let ${\mathcal S}(\R)$ be an o-minimal structure over $\R$, $T \subset \R^{k_1+k_2+\ell}$ a closed definable set, and $$ \displaylines{\pi_1: \R^{k_1+k_2+\ell}\to \R^{k_1 + k_2}, \pi_2: \R^{k_1+k_2+\ell}\to \R^{\ell}, \ \pi_3: \R^{k_1 + k_2} \to \R^{k_2}} $$ the projection maps.   For any collection ${\mathcal A} = \{A_1,...,A_n\}$ of subsets of $\R^{k_1+k_2}$, and $\z \in \R^{k_2}$, let $\A_\z$ denote the collection of subsets of $\R^{k_1}$, $\{A_{1,\z},..., A_{n,\z}\}$, where $A_{i,\z} = A_i \cap \pi_3^{-1}(\z), 1 \leq i \leq n$. We prove that there exists a constant $C = C(T) > 0,$ such that for any family ${\mathcal A} = \{A_1,...,A_n\}$ of definable sets, where each $A_i = \pi_1(T \cap \pi_2^{-1}(\y_i))$, for some $\y_i \in \R^{\ell}$, the number of distinct stable homotopy types of $\A_\z, \z \in \R^{k_2}$, is bounded by $ \displaystyle{C \cdot n^{(k_1+1)k_2},} $ while the number of distinct homotopy types is bounded by $ \displaystyle{C \cdot n^{(k_1+3)k_2}.} $ This generalizes to the general o-minimal setting, bounds of the same type proved in \cite{BV} for semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian families. One main technical tool used in the proof of the above results, is a topological comparison theorem which might be of independent interest in the study of arrangements.

{\mathcal A}_{\mathbf z}=\{A_{1,\mathbf z},\ldots,A_{n,\mathbf z}\},

\[
A_{i,\mathbf z}=A_i\cap \pi_3^{-1}(\mathbf z), \qquad 1\leq i\leq n.

C\cdot n^{(k_1+3)k_2}.

where

A_{i,\mathbf z}=A_i\cap \pi_3^{-1}(\mathbf z),\qquad 1\le i\le n.

We establish the following result. There is a constant \(C=C(T)>0\) such that, for every family \({\mathcal A}=\{A_1,\ldots,A_n\}\) of definable sets with each member of the form

\[
C\, n^{(k_1+3)k_2}.

These estimates extend to arbitrary o-minimal structures bounds of the same form previously obtained in \cite{BV} for semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian families. A key ingredient in the proof is a topological comparison theorem for arrangements, which may also be useful in its own right.

The text investigates families of definable sets in an o-minimal structure over \(\mathbb{R}\). These families are constructed in a uniform way from a fixed closed definable set \(T\). More precisely, the sets under consideration arise as projections of fibers of \(T\), so that all members of the family are controlled by the same underlying definable data. This framework allows the authors to study how the topology of the resulting sets varies as certain parameters change.

For each parameter \(\mathbf{z} \in \mathbb{R}^{k_2}\), the authors consider a collection \(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbf{z}}\) of subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^{k_1}\). This collection is obtained by taking the fibers over \(\mathbf{z}\) of a fixed finite list of definable sets \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\). Thus, for every choice of \(\mathbf{z}\), one obtains an arrangement of \(n\) definable sets in \(\mathbb{R}^{k_1}\). The main question is how many different topological types can occur among these arrangements as the parameter \(\mathbf{z}\) varies.

The first main result concerns stable homotopy types. The authors prove that the number of distinct stable homotopy types of the arrangements \(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbf{z}}\) is bounded by  
\[
C \cdot n^{(k_1+1)k_2},
\]
where the constant \(C\) depends only on the fixed definable set \(T\), and not on \(n\) or on the parameter \(\mathbf{z}\). In other words, although the parameter space may contain infinitely many possible values of \(\mathbf{z}\), only polynomially many stable homotopy types can actually occur, with an exponent determined by the dimensions \(k_1\) and \(k_2\).

The authors also establish a corresponding result for ordinary homotopy types. In this case, the number of distinct homotopy types of the arrangements \(\mathcal{A}_{\mathbf{z}}\) is bounded by  
\[
C \cdot n^{(k_1+3)k_2}.
\]
This is a slightly weaker bound than the one for stable homotopy types, reflected in the larger exponent. Nevertheless, it still shows that the topological complexity of the family grows at most polynomially in the number \(n\) of sets in the arrangement.

These results extend earlier bounds that were known for more specific categories, such as semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian families. The significance of the work is that it places these phenomena in the much broader setting of o-minimal structures, where definable sets retain many of the finiteness and tameness properties familiar from real algebraic and analytic geometry. A key ingredient in the proofs is a topological comparison theorem, which allows the authors to relate the homotopy or stable homotopy type of one definable construction to another more manageable one. This comparison makes it possible to transfer combinatorial bounds on parameter spaces into bounds on the number of distinct topological types.

This work investigates the topology of arrangements of definable sets in an arbitrary o-minimal structure. More precisely, it considers finite families of sets that arise as fibers of definable sets under coordinate projections, and studies how the homotopy types of the resulting arrangements change as the parameters defining the fibers vary. The central problem is to give uniform quantitative bounds on the number of different topological types that can occur in such parameterized families.

The main tool is a framework of projection-defined families. Starting with a fixed definable set in a higher-dimensional ambient space, one obtains a family of subsets of Euclidean space by projecting onto selected coordinates and allowing the remaining coordinates to serve as parameters. Given several such families, one can form arrangements by taking all Boolean combinations, unions, intersections, or other naturally associated regions determined by the fibers. The question is then how many different homotopy types these regions can have as the parameters vary.

A key ingredient in the argument is a topological comparison theorem. This theorem allows one to compare the homotopy type of a definable set with that of a related set obtained through a controlled approximation or projection procedure. In particular, it provides a way to replace complicated definable fibers by more manageable objects without changing their homotopy type, or at least without changing their stable homotopy type. This makes it possible to transfer combinatorial and topological information from the parameter space to the fibers of the arrangement.

Using these methods, the text proves that the number of distinct stable homotopy types arising in such definable arrangements is bounded polynomially in the number of sets in the arrangement, with constants depending only on the defining family and on the ambient dimensions. It also establishes corresponding polynomial bounds for ordinary homotopy types under suitable hypotheses. These bounds show that, although the parameter space may be large and the individual fibers may vary in complicated ways, the number of topologically different possibilities is controlled in a uniform and polynomial manner.

The results extend earlier theorems known in more restrictive settings, especially for semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian sets. In those cases, polynomial bounds on the number of possible homotopy types had been obtained using algebraic or analytic complexity measures such as degrees, formats, and Pfaffian chains. The present work shows that the same kind of phenomenon holds much more generally in the o-minimal context, where definability replaces explicit algebraic or Pfaffian descriptions. Thus the paper places these previous results in a broader model-theoretic and topological framework.

Overall, the text demonstrates that o-minimality provides enough tameness to ensure strong finiteness properties for arrangements of definable sets. Even without relying on specific algebraic equations or inequalities, one can still obtain effective qualitative bounds on the variation of topology in definable families. The main contribution is therefore both a generalization of known bounds and a conceptual clarification of why such bounds hold: they follow from the controlled behavior of definable families under projection, together with robust topological comparison results.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a LaTeX-style abstract for a paper proving polynomial bounds on the number of stable homotopy types and homotopy types of fibers in arrangements of definable sets in an o-minimal structure.
counterfactuals.output:
\[
\textbf{Abstract}
\]
We prove polynomial upper bounds for the number of distinct homotopy types of fibers arising in finite arrangements of definable sets in an o-minimal structure. More precisely, given a fixed definable family
\[
\{S_y \subset \mathbb{R}^k : y \in \mathbb{R}^\ell\},
\]
we show that, for any collection of \(n\) members of the family, the number of stable homotopy types realized by the fibers of all Boolean combinations in the induced arrangement is bounded by a polynomial in \(n\), whose degree depends only on the ambient dimensions and the defining family. Under natural additional hypotheses, the same polynomial bound holds for ordinary homotopy types.

The proof combines Hardt triviality in the o-minimal setting with quantitative stratification and combinatorial bounds for arrangements. A key ingredient is a uniform control of the topology of parameter fibers via definable trivializations, allowing one to reduce the enumeration of possible homotopy types to the enumeration of cells in a definable decomposition of parameter space. These results extend classical bounds for semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian families to arbitrary o-minimal structures, and show that the topological complexity of definable arrangements grows at most polynomially with the size of the arrangement, for fixed defining data.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an academic abstract generalizing Basu–Vorobjov type bounds from semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian families to arbitrary o-minimal structures, including the setup with projections \(\pi_1,\pi_2,\pi_3\) and a closed definable parameter set \(T\).
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract.**  
We formulate an o-minimal analogue of Basu–Vorobjov type finiteness bounds for definable families. Let \(\mathcal R\) be an arbitrary o-minimal expansion of a real closed field and let  
\[
T\subset R^{k_{1}+k_{2}+\ell}
\]
be a closed definable set. We write
\[
\pi_{1}:R^{k_{1}+k_{2}+\ell}\to R^{k_{1}+k_{2}},\qquad
\pi_{2}:R^{k_{1}+k_{2}+\ell}\to R^{\ell},
\]
for the projections onto the first \(k_{1}+k_{2}\) and last \(\ell\) coordinates, respectively, and
\[
\pi_{3}:R^{k_{1}+k_{2}+\ell}\to R^{k_{2}+\ell}
\]
for the projection forgetting the first \(k_{1}\) coordinates. For each parameter \(y\in R^{\ell}\), set
\[
T_{y}:=\pi_{1}\bigl(T\cap \pi_{2}^{-1}(y)\bigr)\subset R^{k_{1}+k_{2}},
\]
and consider the fibers of the induced projection \(T_y\to R^{k_2}\). We prove that, as \(y\) varies in \(R^{\ell}\) and the base point varies in \(R^{k_{2}}\), only finitely many definable homotopy types of such fibers occur.

The result extends the qualitative content of the Basu–Vorobjov bounds from semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian families to arbitrary o-minimal structures. In the semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian settings, the number of possible homotopy types can be bounded explicitly in terms of the usual combinatorial data, such as the number and degrees of defining polynomials or the Pfaffian format. In a general o-minimal structure, no intrinsic notion of degree or format is available; nevertheless, o-minimal triviality and definable stratification yield a uniform finiteness theorem. More precisely, there exists a finite definable partition of the parameter space \(R^{k_{2}+\ell}\) such that over each part the corresponding fibers are definably homeomorphic, and hence have the same definable homotopy type.

This provides a common conceptual framework for Basu–Vorobjov type theorems: the quantitative estimates in the semi-algebraic and semi-Pfaffian cases arise from effective bounds on the complexity of such partitions, while the underlying finiteness phenomenon follows from o-minimality alone.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: State a theorem-like summary about arrangements \(\mathcal A=\{A_i\}\) of definable sets \(A_i=\pi_1(T\cap\pi_2^{-1}(y_i))\), describing bounds \(C n^{(k_1+1)k_2}\) for stable homotopy types and \(C n^{(k_1+3)k_2}\) for homotopy types of sliced arrangements \(\mathcal A_z\).
counterfactuals.output:
**Theorem (Uniform bounds for definable arrangements and sliced arrangements).**  
Let \(T\) be a fixed definable set in an o-minimal structure, and let
\[
\pi_1,\pi_2
\]
be the coordinate projections such that, for each parameter \(y\), the set
\[
A_y=\pi_1\bigl(T\cap \pi_2^{-1}(y)\bigr)
\]
is a definable subset of the ambient space. For any choice of parameters
\[
y_1,\dots,y_n,
\]
let
\[
\mathcal A=\{A_i\}_{i=1}^n,\qquad 
A_i=\pi_1\bigl(T\cap \pi_2^{-1}(y_i)\bigr),
\]
be the corresponding arrangement of definable sets.

Then there exists a constant \(C>0\), depending only on the defining data \(T,\pi_1,\pi_2\) and not on \(n\), such that the number of distinct **stable homotopy types** arising from the realizations of the arrangement \(\mathcal A\) is bounded by
\[
C\, n^{(k_1+1)k_2}.
\]

Moreover, if one considers the associated **sliced arrangements**
\[
\mathcal A_z
\]
obtained by restricting the members of \(\mathcal A\) to fibers or slices indexed by a parameter \(z\), then the number of distinct ordinary **homotopy types** realized by the sliced arrangements \(\mathcal A_z\), as \(z\) varies, is bounded by
\[
C\, n^{(k_1+3)k_2}.
\]

In particular, for a fixed definable family, the topological complexity of arrangements grows polynomially in the number \(n\) of members, with exponents depending only on the relevant ambient and parameter dimensions \(k_1\) and \(k_2\), and not on the particular choice of parameters \(y_1,\dots,y_n\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

We study arrangements of definable sets in a fixed o-minimal expansion of the real field.  Let \(k_{1},k_{2}\geq 0\), let  
\[
\pi_{1}:\mathbb R^{k_{1}+k_{2}}\to \mathbb R^{k_{1}},\qquad   
\pi_{2}:\mathbb R^{k_{1}+k_{2}}\to \mathbb R^{k_{2}}
\]
denote the coordinate projections, and, for a definable set \(S\subset \mathbb R^{k_{1}+k_{2}}\) and a parameter \(y\in \mathbb R^{k_{2}}\), write  
\[
S_{y}:=\pi_{1}\bigl(S\cap \pi_{2}^{-1}(y)\bigr)
      =\{x\in \mathbb R^{k_{1}}:(x,y)\in S\}
\]
for the fiber of \(S\) over \(y\).  Given a finite definable family  
\[
\mathcal A=\{S_{1},\ldots,S_{n}\}
\]
in \(\mathbb R^{k_{1}+k_{2}}\), we consider the induced arrangements on the fibers \(\mathbb R^{k_{1}}\), namely the collections  
\[
\mathcal A_{y}=\{(S_{1})_{y},\ldots,(S_{n})_{y}\},\qquad y\in\mathbb R^{k_{2}},
\]
together with the cells and Boolean combinations determined by these sets.  The central question is how the topology of these fiberwise arrangements varies with the parameter \(y\).  Our main results give uniform bounds, depending only on the o-minimal complexity data of the defining family and on \(k_{1},k_{2},n\), for the number of distinct homotopy types that can occur among the fibers and among the realizations of sign or membership conditions of the arrangements \(\mathcal A_{y}\) as \(y\) ranges over \(\mathbb R^{k_{2}}\).  In particular, for families of bounded format, the number of possible homotopy types is bounded effectively—indeed polynomially in \(n\) for fixed ambient dimensions and format—extending classical finiteness phenomena for semi-algebraic arrangements to the o-minimal setting.
